unit.why: A first-person memorate told by the tsaddik: as a boy he declined his grandfather's offer to teach him kabbalah and to give him holy minds during prayer, preferring his own effort, and later dreamt that his master brought him tefillin from Gan Eden.

stories.start_quote: סיפר לי חסיד מופלג א׳ ששמע מפיו
stories.summary_en: As an eleven-year-old the tsaddik declined his grandfather the Maggid's offers to teach him kabbalah and to give him holy minds during prayer, wanting to attain them by his own worship; later he saw in a night vision his master the Ohev Yisrael bring him tefillin housings from Gan Eden, signifying the holy minds he had earned by his own service.

quotes: קרא אותי אא״ז ז״ל ואמר לי
tags.why: His grandfather, the Maggid, is a central character.
The story turns on study, offered by the grandfather and done alone by the boy.

quotes: בני תהיה בכל יום בשעת תפלת
הייתי רק בהתחלת תפלתו ובסיום תפלתו
tags.why: The boy is present at his grandfather's prayer.
A scene is set in the study hall.

quotes: אשר מורו ורבו ז"ל, הוא ההק׳ בעל אוהב ישראל
tags.why: The story is about receiving from masters, both his grandfather and his teacher.

quotes: שראה בחלון לילה אשר מורו ורבו ז"ל
tags.why: A night vision, likely a dream (the printed בחלון probably stands for חזיון), is given an interpretation (פתרון).

quotes: הביא בתים של תפלין מג״ע ונתן לו
tags.why: Tefillin from Gan Eden are the central symbol of the vision.

quotes: הביא בתים של תפלין מג״ע ונתן לו
tags.why: His deceased master appears to him in the vision.

quotes: סיפר לי חסיד מופלג א׳ ששמע מפיו הק׳
tags.why: The story is framed as told by the tsaddik himself and passed on by a hasid.
The story illustrates his virtue of attaining by his own service rather than by what others give him.

quotes: כי אנכי רציתי להשיג ע״פ עבודתי בעצמי
tags.why: His self-reliance in serving God is presented as praiseworthy.
He does not follow his grandfather's instruction, though without bad consequences.
Default tag; no woman appears in the story.

missing_concepts: spiritual attainment by one's own effort versus receiving it from a tsaddik
mochin (expanded consciousness) transmitted by a tsaddik
